concepts.title: Continuity at a Point
concepts.definition: A function is continuous at an input c of its domain when the limit it approaches at c matches the value it actually takes there; if the left approach, right approach and the value all agree, the graph can be traced through c in one stroke.
concepts.formula: limit of f at c equals f(c) for continuity at c
concepts.key_idea: Limit equals value at the point; any mismatch marks a break.

concepts.title: Discontinuity Points of a Piecewise Function
concepts.definition: For a function defined by different rules on adjoining intervals, the only suspects are the join points: continuity survives there exactly when the left approach and the right approach deliver the same number.
concepts.formula: continuity at a join needs the left limit to equal the right limit
concepts.key_idea: Compare one-sided limits at each branch boundary to locate breaks.

concepts.title: Algebra and Composition of Continuous Functions
concepts.definition: Sums, differences, products and quotients (denominator non-zero) of functions that are continuous at a point stay continuous there, and chaining two continuous functions keeps continuity through the composition.
concepts.formula: f plus g, f times g and f of g are continuous wherever f and g are

concepts.title: Differentiability and One-Sided Derivatives
concepts.definition: A function is differentiable at c when the difference quotient limit exists finitely, which means the left and right difference quotients agree; every differentiable function is automatically continuous, yet continuity alone is not enough, as the modulus function shows at the origin.
concepts.formula: f_prime(c) = limit of (f(c + h) - f(c)) / h as h tends to 0
concepts.key_idea: Equal finite one-sided difference quotients are the differentiability test; corners break it.

solution_steps.action: Form the difference quotient from the left
solution_steps.explain: Take the limit of (f(c + h) - f(c)) / h with h negative.

solution_steps.action: Form the difference quotient from the right
solution_steps.explain: Repeat with h positive.
Equal finite values give differentiability; unequal values (as for |x| at 0) refuse it.
Differentiability at c guarantees continuity at c, never the reverse.

concepts.title: Chain Rule for Composite Functions
concepts.definition: To differentiate a function nested inside another, multiply the outer derivative (evaluated at the inner expression) by the inner derivative; with deeper nesting the products keep stacking.
concepts.formula: df/dx = dv/dt times dt/dx where t is the inner function
concepts.key_idea: Differentiate outside first, then inside, and multiply the rates.

concepts.title: Derivatives of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
concepts.definition: Each inverse trigonometric function has a standard derivative on its principal branch: arcsine and arccosine give plus or minus one over the square root of one minus x squared, while arctangent and arccotangent give plus or minus one over one plus x squared.
concepts.formula: d/dx of sin inverse x equals 1 / sqrt(1 - x**2) on (-1, 1)
concepts.key_idea: Memorise the four standard inverse trig derivatives with their domains.
concepts.textbook_ref: lemh105.txt section 5.3.3 with example 24 and summary table (lines ~2298-2376, 5264-5306)

concepts.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
concepts.definition: Raising a base bigger than one to a variable power gives the exponential function, defined on all reals with positive outputs; its inverse, the logarithm, answers the question of which exponent the base needs to produce a given positive number.
concepts.formula: log base b of a equals x exactly when b raised to x equals a
concepts.key_idea: Exponential and logarithm undo each other; e is the natural base.

solution_steps.explain: b to the x equals a mirrors log base b of a equals x.
